A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Aux-Think study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices A.1–A.5 are readable and support reliable comparison despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original navigation results on R2R-CE and RxR-CE, component and planning-horizon ablations, cross-dataset evaluation, and qualitative reinforcement-learning outcomes.

after.justification: v3 retains original navigation experiments and supplementary results, reports revised results with expanded training data, and adds analysis of the R2R-CoT-320k corpus.

M1.justification: The NVILA-lite 8B model, auxiliary CoT and instruction-reconstruction tasks, prompt switching, and receding-horizon inference remain unchanged. Equation (4)'s index correction aligns the formula with the existing procedural description rather than introducing a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Section 4.3 adds a separately identified 500K web-data source to Aux-Think training, although its corpus and task composition are unspecified. R2R-CE, RxR-CE, and cross-dataset evaluation coverage remain unchanged. DAgger data already appeared in v1.

E2.justification: Table 1 removes the NaVid comparison using 180K extra training examples, whose SR was 37.4. NaVid with zero extra data remains there, and its cross-dataset comparison remains in Table 6. Other comparator memberships are unchanged.

E3.justification: The principal scaled-training configuration changes from 600K extra RxR examples to 600K RxR, 500K DAgger, and 500K web examples, increasing total training data from 920K to 1920K. The separate 180K-extra-data comparison also disappears. Evaluation splits, navigation metrics, model size, and stated training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 adds vocabulary-frequency and reasoning-length analyses of the existing dataset through Figure 5's word cloud and histogram. Component, planning-horizon, CoT-loss-weight, and trajectory-length analyses, the navigation case study, and RL investigations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for navigation results. The new corpus-frequency and length plots are descriptive dataset analyses rather than changed uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: For (NE, OSR, SR, SPL), Table 1 replaces Aux-Think's (5.88, 54.9, 49.7, 41.7) with (6.08, 60.0, 54.8, 46.9); Table 2 replaces (6.91, 60.1, 49.3, 37.9) with (6.24, 61.9, 52.2, 40.2). These use different training mixtures, not identical settings. The 180K comparison rows disappear, and Figure 5 adds corpus findings; Tables 3–7 retain their results.

T1.justification: Equation (4) changes the target action index from t+n to t+k inside the sum over k, correcting the mathematical objective to agree with its existing explanation. Other equations and formal content remain unchanged; neither version adds theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces best performance 'under the same data scale' with best navigation success rate, and the introduction adds this SR claim to the contributions. Section 4.3 likewise shifts from comparable performance to SOTA SR. This materially changes the headline comparison's scope, while retaining the IRC, method, and dataset contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.2 newly interprets frequent spatial terms as evidence of navigation-semantic alignment and varied reasoning lengths as evidence of complexity and greater challenge than short-form static-task CoT datasets. Existing explanations of reasoning collapse, exploration, planning failures, and RL limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page URL and clarifies that Figure 1a excludes receding-horizon planning and Figure 1b's smaller Aux-Think variant uses only R2R-CoT-320k. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, action definitions, and prompts are retained. The PDFs do not establish what resources the new link actually provides.

R1.justification: The 65 references and Related Work section are retained. Appendix A.2 nevertheless adds a limited positioning claim that the dataset poses greater challenges than typical short-form CoT datasets for static tasks.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized abstract and results edits, improved dual-process wording, revised author affiliation and internship text, and added dataset-description paragraphs. The section hierarchy and most prose remain intact; there is no extensive narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: v3 adds the two-panel Figure 5, revises Figure 1's captions and training-data plot, removes Table 1's 180K comparison block, and enlarges Table 2. Other displays mainly shift with text reflow. Section 4.4 incorrectly changes its step-count-analysis reference to Figure 5, although that analysis remains Figure 4.

improvement.justification: The dataset characterization, Equation (4) correction, and expanded-training results improve documentation and evidence. However, v3 loses one direct matched-data comparison and broadens its headline to best SR without clearly restricting it to monocular large-model comparators; Tables 1–2 also list higher-SR panoramic systems. The new web data are only named and sized, and a figure-reference error is introduced. These benefits and losses do not establish a reliable net quality direction.
